# Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling — facts

> Source-anchored units about Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling: 18 across 3 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 18 units · 3 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] Reactive autoscaling responds to sustained resource usage within configured minimum and maximum tiers. Predictive autoscaling attempts to upscale ahead of recurring demand and falls back to reactive scaling for unexpected spikes; neither mechanism guarantees immediate capacity for arbitrary bursts. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling.md
- [statement] A separate scale-up trigger applies to dedicated M10+ operational nodes when Queued or Rejected Operations stays above zero at every sample for ten minutes. Brief overload bursts do not meet this criterion. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling
- [statement] Automatic scaling can miss sudden workload bursts because backing resources take time to prepare. MongoDB advises scaling ahead of bulk inserts or other expected spikes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] For M30+ operational nodes, reactive scale-up criteria include CPU or memory above 90% for ten minutes, or above 75% for one hour, subject to tier bounds and recent scaling cooldowns. These thresholds are documented policy, not an instantaneous response guarantee. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling
- [statement] The Weighted Average independently recommends evaluating busy and quiet workload periods and the complete bill. Its arithmetic interprets a 189% throughput-per-dollar improvement as 2.89 times the baseline, not a 189% cost reduction; any implied savings depend on reproducing the tested performance relationship. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-30) — https://theweightedaverage.com/posts/2026-09-30-atlas-infinite-agent-migration-gates/ · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Compute and storage-capacity separation does not make storage performance independently configurable: Infinite storage IOPS and throughput vary with compute tier, and documented per-tier values cannot be changed within a tier. Storage-bound demand can still require a more expensive compute tier. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling · also: https://theweightedaverage.com/posts/2026-09-30-atlas-infinite-agent-migration-gates/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-landing.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The minimum oplog retention window does not gate Atlas Infinite autoscaling, unlike the oplog-window gate documented for Atlas Core. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling
- [statement] MongoDB’s September 30 launch post claims more than 96% shorter read-scaling time versus Atlas Core and 189% more throughput per dollar. These are vendor performance claims, not measured end-to-end autoscaling response times or universal customer savings. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/ai-demand-constant-unpredictable-extreme-mongodb-is-built-for-it · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling · also: https://theweightedaverage.com/posts/2026-09-30-atlas-infinite-agent-migration-gates/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Predictive eligibility requires General or Low-CPU M30-or-larger clusters, autoscaling enabled, and at least two weeks of activity. If downscaling is enabled, its minimum must remain M30 or larger. Predictive scaling applies to electable and read-only nodes, excluding analytics nodes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling
- [statement] The predictive model examines primary-node resource usage over a rolling four-week window. Monthly or quarterly cycles fall outside that window, and pausing requires two consecutive weeks of activity before predictive scaling resumes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling
- [statement] Predictive scaling increases by at most two tiers per event and respects configured tier bounds. It provides no predictive downscaling; reductions use reactive scaling. A predictive increase scheduled within one hour suppresses reactive downscaling. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling
- [statement] Compute resizing does not move stored data. Additional read-only nodes access shared storage without initial synchronization and are documented to start serving reads in minutes. Adding read nodes is a separate capacity action from automatic tier resizing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-08) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-landing.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling · also: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/ground-beneath-database
- [statement] Compute is billed hourly for the configured tier of a primary-and-standby HA pair plus additional nodes, including idle provisioned nodes. Autoscaling cost estimates must reflect time spent at each tier; independent storage, backup and transfer charges remain separate. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/atlas-infinite-costs.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling · also: https://theweightedaverage.com/posts/2026-09-30-atlas-infinite-agent-migration-gates/
- [statement] Atlas lets customers select minimum and maximum compute tiers and opt out of compute autoscaling; scaling stays within the same General or Low-CPU class. The minimum must accommodate the workload, and the maximum limits the capacity autoscaling can supply. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling
- [statement] Public-preview availability limits Infinite to supported AWS regions and M10–M60 General or M40–M60 Low-CPU replica sets; M80+, sharded clusters and independent/asymmetric shard autoscaling are unsupported. The preview carries no uptime SLA. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-landing.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling
- [statement] The MongoDB engineering article describes a compute swap completing in under a minute and read replicas serving in seconds. These architecture statements do not include reactive detection windows or establish an end-to-end autoscaling latency SLA. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-08) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/ground-beneath-database · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md
- [statement] Atlas Infinite separates compute from managed storage. Changing the compute tier does not require copying the underlying dataset; cluster-tier autoscaling can therefore change compute capacity without increasing stored-data capacity. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-infinite.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-landing.md, https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/ground-beneath-database
- [statement] In TechTarget’s September 29 reporting, Omdia analyst Stephen Catanzano assessed Infinite’s elasticity as a significant addition for unpredictable demand. This is independent analyst opinion; the article attributes its throughput comparisons to MongoDB testing and provides no independent autoscaling timing experiment. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-29) — https://www.techtarget.com/news/Evolving-MongoDB-targets-managing-agents-performance-for-AI/842047/ · keywords: Atlas Infinite compute auto-scaling
